sc-ag-comm-2026-blanding-deshawn.name: DeShawn Blanding
sc-ag-comm-2026-blanding-deshawn.bio: Food and agriculture policy advocate, cooperative business leader and beginning farmer; former U.S. House senior policy staffer and president of AgQuity Solutions.

positions.stance: Lists grounding principles: "Increase access. Lower costs. Simpler government. Local solutions. Secure farms. Secure food."
Pillar 1 of his Rooted Forward plan: "Building locally-rooted jobs and farm infrastructure."
Pillar 2 of his plan, Partnerships: "Expanding farm-to-table purchasing."
Pillar 3 of his plan, Protection: "Keeping our food safe and our working lands."

al-ag-2026-mclaughlin-jeff.name: Jeff McLaughlin
al-ag-2026-mclaughlin-jeff.bio: Guntersville attorney for more than thirty years and former schoolteacher; represented Marshall County in the Alabama House of Representatives for ten years.

positions.stance: Will root out public corruption and hold the powerful accountable "regardless of party or connections."
Will use the office to protect consumers from scams and fraud, crack down on those who prey on the vulnerable, and stand up for victims.
Will support local police, sheriffs and first responders and go after threats including "the flood of fentanyl and dangerous drugs into our state."
Will defend Alabama's people, natural resources and tax dollars "from anyone trying to take advantage of them."
Will apply the law fairly and honestly, "refusing to use the office to settle political scores."

al-ag-2026-robertson-katherine.name: Katherine Robertson
al-ag-2026-robertson-katherine.bio: Chief Counsel to Alabama Attorney General Steve Marshall; former vice president of the Alabama Policy Institute and counsel to Senator Jeff Sessions.

positions.stance: As Attorney General, would "Support President Trump's America First vision from Montgomery."
Would "Defend Alabama's Constitution and sovereignty from Washington's overreach."
Would "Protect the God-given rights of our citizens."
Would "Stop the Left's war on women, faith, and family."
Would "Stand up for free speech and religious freedom."

al-sos-2026-rogers-wayne.name: Wayne Rogers
al-sos-2026-rogers-wayne.bio: Attorney and former federal prosecutor with two decades in private practice.

positions.stance: The Secretary of State "must be an impartial scorekeeper"; will ensure elections are conducted fairly, in a nonpartisan fashion and according to law.
Will work to explain the importance of voting and "expand opportunities to cast ballots to all those who are eligible to do so."
Says Alabama needs "politicians who put people over party" and who will do the right thing even against party bosses.

al-sos-2026-dobson-caroleene.name: Caroleene Dobson
al-sos-2026-dobson-caroleene.bio: Attorney and shareholder at the Maynard Nexsen law firm and commissioner on the Alabama Forestry Commission.

positions.stance: As Secretary of State, "I will reduce fees on Alabama businesses."
Will "streamline services for the public."
Will "never back down from the liberal activist groups who want to undermine the security of our elections."

al-treas-2026-houston-rosilyn.name: Rosilyn Houston
al-treas-2026-houston-rosilyn.bio: Banking executive with thirty years in retail, wealth and commercial banking, including leading BBVA Compass's East Retail Region.

positions.stance: Will safeguard the Alabama Trust Fund, manage the state's cash and debt with discipline, and ensure public deposits are fully secured.
Will publish the office's investment decisions, performance and costs "in plain language."
Will make financial education a working priority of the Treasury, partnering with schools, churches and community groups in all 67 counties.
Will manage investments for "the strongest, safest return for the people who own the money. Not politics, not favors, not fashion."
Will make sure Alabamians know about CollegeCounts, Alabama ABLE and unclaimed property "and can get to their own money without a fight."

al-treas-2026-boozer-young.name: Young Boozer
al-treas-2026-boozer-young.bio: Alabama State Treasurer since 2011; former Executive Vice President at Colonial BancGroup.

al-aud-2026-edwards-violet.name: Violet Edwards
al-aud-2026-edwards-violet.bio: Madison County Commissioner since 2020 and businesswoman; former television and radio news reporter.

positions.stance: Says the office must ensure "taxpayer dollars and state property are accurately accounted for and responsibly managed."
Says making qualified appointments to the Board of Registrars "is essential for strengthening public confidence."
Will work to ensure the Auditor's office "serves ALL Alabamians."

al-aud-2026-sorrell-andrew.name: Andrew Sorrell
al-aud-2026-sorrell-andrew.bio: Alabama State Auditor since 2022, entrepreneur, and former State Representative for House District 3.

positions.stance: Will push legislation letting the office determine negligent loss of state property and open a new Property Investigations Division.
Will seek to rename and expand the Voter Registration Advisory Board as the Voter Registration and Election Integrity Advisory Board.
Believes registrars should earn at least $150 per day with benefits, and will push to raise poll worker pay by at least $25.
Wants to spearhead an "Alabama DOGE" effort to identify and eliminate wasteful spending of taxpayer dollars.
Will continue appointing registrars "serious about election integrity" and "replacing underperforming registrars."

al-ag-ind-2026-sparks-ron.name: Ron Sparks
al-ag-ind-2026-sparks-ron.bio: Former two-term Alabama Commissioner of Agriculture and Industries; former senior advisor to U.S. Senator Doug Jones.

positions.stance: Calls ensuring the safety of food "one of my primary responsibilities" and cites his past country-of-origin labeling requirements on imported food.
Says animal abuse "is a heinous crime, and one that we should not tolerate in Alabama."
Will bring back full inspection and certification of every gasoline pump: "You pay for a gallon, you get a gallon of gas."
"I will vigorously investigate price gouging" and enforce the rules to the maximum extent the law allows.
Supports eliminating Alabama's 1.5% sales tax on farm equipment to provide relief to farmers.

al-ag-ind-2026-hill-corey.name: Corey Hill
al-ag-ind-2026-hill-corey.bio: Mayor of Douglas, grocery store operator, and cattle and poultry farmer.

al-psc1-2026-gordon-james.name: James O. Gordon
al-psc1-2026-gordon-james.bio: Chiropractor and Mobile business owner; former member of the Alabama House of Representatives for District 98 (2006-2010).

positions.stance: Believes in protecting consumers and ensuring utilities "operate fairly, transparently, and in the best interest of everyday citizens."
Platform lists affordability, noting high monthly power bills while "the power company is making billions a year."
Says a commissioner could help small cities find grants for sidewalks, bike trails or community bus service.

al-psc1-2026-gentry-matt.name: Matt Gentry
al-psc1-2026-gentry-matt.bio: Cullman County Sheriff and U.S. Marine Corps veteran.

al-psc2-2026-mcneil-sheila.name: Sheila D. McNeil
al-psc2-2026-mcneil-sheila.bio: Chair of the Madison County Democratic Executive Committee; holds degrees in social work and public administration.

positions.stance: Will "focus on fair rates, reliable service, and transparent decision-making, putting Alabama consumers first."
Committed to "lowering costs, improving reliability, and ensuring fair treatment for all Alabama utility customers."

al-psc2-2026-zeigler-jim.name: Jim Zig Zeigler
al-psc2-2026-zeigler-jim.bio: Former Alabama State Auditor (2015-2023), former Public Service Commission member, and elder care attorney.

positions.stance: Will insist on cost allocation that protects residential ratepayers: "If Big Tech creates the power shock, Big Tech should fund the power solution."
Will thoroughly review rate requests, ask detailed questions, and ensure transparency in how costs are recovered from ratepayers.
Will apply consistent oversight standards to gas utilities, ensuring rate requests are thoroughly reviewed and justified.
Will ensure pipeline inspections are thorough and enforcement consistent: "There are no shortcuts when public safety is at stake."
Will prioritize railroad safety oversight and ensure rail companies maintain safe infrastructure.

ok-ag-2026-echols-jon.name: Jon Echols
ok-ag-2026-echols-jon.bio: Small business owner and former State Representative for House District 90, where he served as House Majority Floor Leader.

positions.stance: "Back the blue: respect law enforcement and our heroes in blue."
Will zealously advocate for Oklahomans' freedoms "while upholding the Judeo Christian values our nation was founded upon."
Will "serve as a watch dog of tax payer dollars."
Will support President Trump "as he secures our borders and defeats the scourge that is fentanyl."
"There should be no tolerance for DEI in the Attorney General's Office."

ok-ag-2026-coffey-nick.name: Nick Coffey
ok-ag-2026-coffey-nick.bio: Federal prosecutor in the Western District of Oklahoma.

positions.stance: Oklahoma "needs to root out corruption in government"; elected officials should be held to a higher standard.
Will crack down on illegal firearms in the wrong hands, fight drug cartels, protect kids from online predators, and protect land from foreign entities.
Says the next AG "needs to take care of Oklahoma's families," including protecting kids from online predators.
Will be "a watch dog for our tax dollars" and expose bad business practices that take money from Oklahomans.

ok-treas-2026-byrd-cindy.name: Cindy Byrd
ok-treas-2026-byrd-cindy.bio: CPA and Oklahoma State Auditor and Inspector since 2019.

positions.stance: Will build on tourism efforts and support policies that help Oklahoma businesses grow, removing "unnecessary state-level barriers."
Wants education spending easier to track, with classroom spending clearly separated from administrative costs and public reporting.
Supports top-to-bottom reviews of state health agencies and keeping "the focus on direct patient care, not bureaucracy."
Says "We need to lead with prevention," prioritizing early intervention and community-based solutions.
Will expand performance audits and require agencies to plan ahead for reduced federal dollars.

ok-supt-2026-franklin-robert.name: Robert Franklin
ok-supt-2026-franklin-robert.bio: Educator for 44 years, former Associate Superintendent at Tulsa Tech, and instructor of future school leaders at OU-Tulsa.

positions.stance: Schools must focus on "reading, math, classroom discipline, and strong academic expectations," including early literacy and numeracy.
Supports parental involvement and transparency; says "Parents deserve a voice in their child's education."
Supports school choice with "high standards, clear accountability" and wise use of education dollars.
Students should graduate with a pathway such as CareerTech, college, apprenticeships, certifications or workforce training.
Supports better professional development and recruitment: "We can be pro-teacher and pro-accountability at the same time."

ok-supt-2026-marshall-jennettie.name: Jennettie Marshall
ok-supt-2026-marshall-jennettie.bio: Pastor and former Tulsa Public Schools Board of Education member; former probation and parole officer and child welfare investigator.

positions.stance: Supports a top-to-bottom review of the OSDE and re-evaluating its spending so taxpayer dollars reach classrooms.
Wants schools focused on reading, writing and math, with rigorous standards "free from political influence."
Says Oklahoma must prioritize raising teacher salaries to be competitive with neighboring states and the national average.
Supports ensuring special education funding reaches students, reducing caseloads, and delivering services in every IEP.
Supports clear performance information for parents and accountability that provides targeted support to struggling schools.

ok-labor-2026-west-kevin.name: Kevin West
ok-labor-2026-west-kevin.bio: State Representative for Oklahoma House District 54 since 2016 and former cabinet shop owner.

positions.stance: Will expand CareerTech partnerships, create apprenticeship incentives, and streamline licensing so qualified workers can start faster.
Will guarantee fair bidding on public contracts and cut outdated rules, mandates and red tape.
Supports "Teach before you fine" safety partnerships with employers and opposes forced union dues.
Will create skilled trade pathways for veterans and training programs for those seeking a second chance.
Will launch a bipartisan task force on AI and automation to protect Oklahoma workers.

ok-labor-2026-dawson-kevin.name: Kevin Dawson
ok-labor-2026-dawson-kevin.bio: Retired locomotive engineer who worked 43 years in the railroad industry, including in training and safety management.

positions.stance: Will apply labor laws fairly and consistently, upholding wage and child labor protections with "no favoritism."
Will give businesses clear guidance and hold bad actors accountable so they cannot undercut those who follow the rules.
Will enforce strong safety standards across every industry, focusing inspections where risk is highest.
Will "Enforce the law without growing government" and make the system faster, clearer and more transparent.

ok-ins-2026-sullivan-bob.name: Bob Sullivan
ok-ins-2026-sullivan-bob.bio: Property and casualty insurance professional with Alera Group; formerly with Rich & Cartmill.

positions.stance: Will take on big insurers, demand transparency, and "fight for lower, fairer rates."
Will make sure insurers pay claims on time, play by the rules, and treat Oklahomans with respect.
Will open the market and recruit strong, reliable carriers so competition works for consumers.
Will fight to make insurance "affordable, predictable, and responsive" for families and entrepreneurs.
Describes himself as "Pro-Life, Pro-2A, and Pro-Business."

ok-ins-2026-macintyre-craig.name: Craig MacIntyre
ok-ins-2026-macintyre-craig.bio: Insurance industry professional for 30+ years, including as an actuary; former educator and small business owner.

positions.stance: All rate filings will be analyzed before taking effect, and rates that are too high "will be rejected."
Will give the OID Consumer Protection Division new authority to examine patterns of unfair claims practices.
Will work with insurers new to Oklahoma to create a fair playing field and more competition.
Will strengthen fraud investigations and not tolerate illegal claims activity that raises everyone's rates.
Legislative priority: make mediation mandatory if requested by either party, to reduce lawsuits and costs.

ok-corp-2026-boles-brad.name: Brad Boles
ok-corp-2026-boles-brad.bio: Businessman and State Representative for Grady and Stephens Counties since 2018; former Mayor of Marlow.

positions.stance: Will ensure fair utility rates, fight unnecessary regulations, and put ratepayers first.
Will defend oil, gas and electric industries "from federal overreach and radical environmental policies."
Will champion policies that grow the energy sector "while protecting our land, water, and air."
Will streamline regulations and cut red tape so the Commission helps private sector growth.
Will "protect Oklahoma families, defend free markets, and keep government accountable."
Warns Oklahoma has over 20,000 documented abandoned oil and gas wells that will fall to the state and taxpayers to close.
Calls injection wells a temporary solution, citing leaking wells that contaminate land and the water table.
Has "huge concerns regarding nuclear power given our extreme weather" as a power source for data centers.
"I am wholeheartedly against the Smelter"; says jobs must fit into existing rural communities.
Says regulation exists to protect the environment, resources and people "from Exploitation and abuse."

ct-sots-2026-thomas-stephanie.name: Stephanie Thomas
ct-sots-2026-thomas-stephanie.bio: Connecticut Secretary of the State since 2023; former State Representative, nonprofit consultant and small business owner.

positions.stance: Will continue implementing election changes "while ensuring that you can vote safely and securely."
Says voters must be inspired to vote and election materials, systems and procedures "must be easy to understand."
Focused on "restoring trust in our government by teaching Connecticut residents how to navigate our government."
Supports sharing resources and training and streamlining the process for Connecticut businesses.
Supports "Reducing taxes and cutting red tape to unleash Connecticut's economic potential."
"Creating an environment where families can thrive and prosper."
"Defending our constitutional rights and conservative principles."
Will keep improving the state's fiscal health and credit rating while investing in housing, "a key to affordability and economic growth."
Will build on pension fund reforms "to further ensure the retirement security of pensioners."
Will strengthen the state's ability to fight back against federal actions targeting "core programs upon which working families depend."

ct-treas-2026-wilms-fred.name: Fred Wilms
ct-treas-2026-wilms-fred.bio: Senior Vice President at Webster Bank; former two-term Connecticut State Representative and chairman of Norwalk's Board of Estimate and Taxation.

positions.stance: Supports reforms prioritizing stable returns and solvency, and creating an Investment Board to share fiduciary responsibility.
Will focus on paying down debt: "borrow only when we must, spend only what we have."
Will proactively disclose investment performance, management fees, and unclaimed property data.
Will resist ESG, hold managers to benchmarks, and publish quarterly performance scorecards.
